hook: A washing machine drum spins up, holds a fast spin, then coasts to a stop. Its edge travels a long way, yet the drum never goes anywhere. To describe turning, physics swaps position, velocity and acceleration for angle, angular velocity and angular acceleration, and every equation you already know comes back with new letters.

figure.caption: A wheel turned through 1 rad: the distance along the rim equals the radius. Each straight-line quantity has a rotational partner.

chain.cause: Every point of a rigid wheel turns together about the axis
chain.effect: one angle θ describes the whole wheel

chain.cause: The angle changes over a time interval
chain.effect: the wheel has an angular velocity ω = Δθ/Δt, in rad/s

chain.cause: The angular velocity changes over a time interval
chain.effect: the wheel has an angular acceleration α = Δω/Δt, in rad/s²
the three kinematic equations hold with θ, ω, α in place of x, v, a

chain.cause: α has the same sign as ω (or the opposite sign)
chain.effect: the wheel speeds up (or slows down)

ideas: Measure angles in radians: θ = (distance along the circle) ÷ r. One revolution = 2π rad = 360°.
Pick a positive direction, usually counterclockwise. Then θ, ω and α carry signs exactly as x, v and a do on a line.
A rigid system turns as one piece: every point shares the same θ, ω and α.
Constant α: ω = ω₀ + αt; θ = θ₀ + ω₀t + ½αt²; ω² = ω₀² + 2αΔθ.
On an ω-t graph the slope is α and the area is Δθ.

misconception.wrong: A point near the rim of a turning wheel has a larger angular velocity than a point near the axle, because it moves faster.
misconception.right: Both points turn through the same angle in the same time, so they share one ω. The point near the rim covers more distance, which is a separate quantity (its speed, next topic).

summary: Rotation about a fixed axis is described by the angle θ in radians, the angular velocity ω = Δθ/Δt and the angular acceleration α = Δω/Δt, each with a sign for clockwise or counterclockwise. Every point of a rigid system shares them, and for constant α the three linear kinematic equations hold with θ, ω and α in place of x, v and a.
